title: Subbing for Sam Woodyard with Ellington; dates with Johnny Hodges
summary: Duke called him when Sam Woodyard did not show, partly because he had played with Mercer, and Hodges used him on record dates.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did you ever know Duke?
Duke Ellington?
Yeah.
Oh, sure. I played with him every time Sam Woodyard wouldn't show up. They'd call me.
I must ask you about that. Don't you love the way Sam Woodyard played, though?
Oh, yeah, sure.
He sounded so good in that band.
He certainly did.
I mean, he'd get high and everything, (unintelligible), but he did suit that band so marvelously.
I think the reason why they called me was because I played with Duke's son.
Mercer?
Mercer.
When did you play with Mercer?
Before -- oh, a long time ago. During the times I wasn't working around in New York, see.
Is that right.
And --
--was Strayhorn with the band? When Mercer was (inaudible).
Oh, no, no, no.
Mercer just had a bunch of kids.
Yeah, he had a bunch of guys he had got together for this band, see.
Yeah.
And I worked in this band about four or five times. And he told Duke about it, and so Duke would call me. And Johnny Hodges would have me on a lot of record dates with him, see.
Oh, really? Now, we haven't talked about that.
Yeah.
Yeah, on those small band dates.
Yeah, they were small band with Johnny Hodges, yeah.
Yeah, beautiful.

Yes, goodness' sake. I loved playing with that guy. And just before he died, I came by the theatre there and said, 'You're just the guy I want to see. I'm making a date three weeks from now.' And he died just before those three weeks. I had a record date with him.
(End of proceedings as recorded.)
